translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Woolf’s conversational, ironic, long-breathed sentences are kept in flowing literary Vietnamese, with the audience addressed as ‘các bạn’ and the narrator as ‘tôi’.
decisions.rationale: The essay is a spoken argument whose irony lives in sentence rhythm.

decisions.decision: The English letter ‘I’ is glossed once in the text; ‘Lady’ is ‘phu nhân’; women in the generic sense are ‘nàng’ and Mary Carmichael ‘cô’.
decisions.rationale: One rendering per term; English-specific images need a short gloss.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘every other man’ was halved into ‘one in two’; restored to its full claim.
‘I doubt whether that was true of Charlotte Brontë’ was rendered as its opposite; corrected.
‘a whole nine years ago’ lost its irony (‘mới đây đúng chín năm’); now ‘đã trọn chín năm rồi’.
The English capital letter ‘I’, Woolf’s emblem of male egotism, was left unexplained; a short gloss was added.
Dash and quote styles drifted from unit 114; normalised to the source; ‘Lady’, ‘sitting-room’ and the generic-woman pronoun unified.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.source_term: a room of one’s own / five hundred a year
glossary.draft_rendering: một căn phòng riêng / năm trăm bảng một năm
glossary.rationale: The essay’s thesis phrase and its income figure, rendered identically at every occurrence.
Coventry Patmore’s title, used by Woolf for the ideal of selfless womanhood.

glossary.source_term: the letter ‘I’ (the shadow of the male ego)
glossary.draft_rendering: chữ ‘I’ with a bracketed gloss at first use
glossary.rationale: English-specific emblem: in English the first person is a single capital letter; a short gloss lets the image of the dark bar work.

glossary.source_term: Mary Beton, Mary Seton, Mary Carmichael; Oxbridge, Fernham
glossary.rationale: Woolf’s narrator names and invented colleges are kept.

witness_decision: Selected the Project Gutenberg Australia electronic text (file 0200791h) of A Room of One's Own, first published by the Hogarth Press in London in 1929. The transcription’s underlying printing is not stated on the page and the text was not collated with the 1929 edition.

unresolved_questions.explanation: A few phrases remain slightly literal (for example the rendering of ‘uneducated’ in the last chapter).

title_review.rationale: Một căn phòng riêng is the established Vietnamese title of the essay.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening: ‘But, you may say, we asked you to speak about women and fiction’.
The closing appeal about the poet who would come if we worked for her.
